set.typical_award_size: Requirement, not a subsidy. Ordinance 24-OR0004-1 (introduced January 24, 2024, adopted February 14, 2024, effective outside the Coastal Zone) raised the set-aside from 10 to 15 percent, added unit mix, dispersal and equal amenity rules for reserved units, and clarified ADU use. The Coastal Commission approved the amendment on February 5, 2026 (LCP-6-OCN-25-0030-2) with seven suggested modifications. The City Council introduced an ordinance adopting the modifications on June 3, 2026 (5-0) and adopted it June 17, 2026; it applies citywide. Current rules: applies to residential projects of 7 or more units (including mixed-use, condo conversions and time extensions); at least 15 percent of units reserved (for-sale units for lower and moderate income, rental units for lower income); acutely low income category added; affordability for at least 55 years for rental and for-sale; ADUs may satisfy the requirement in any residential project; affordable housing agreement recorded before building permit, final map or Coastal Development Permit. In-lieu fee per reserved unit is set by Council resolution, deferrable on impact fee terms, and deposited in the affordable housing trust account. Rental projects have been covered since the September 9, 2020 Phase 1 amendment.
set.affordability_requirement: 15 percent of base units (density bonus units excluded): for-sale units for lower and moderate income households, rental units for lower income households; minimum 55 year restrictions for rental and for-sale units.
eligible_project_detail: market-rate rental and for-sale projects of 7 or more units (compliance)
set.next_deadline: Applies at entitlement. Confirm the current in-lieu fee rate with the Housing Division.
set.cycle_notes: Ongoing requirement; Coastal Commission modifications adopted citywide June 17, 2026.
set.layering_notes: In-lieu fee revenue is Oceanside's only recurring local housing fund; the Housing Element lists inclusionary fees with HOME, Housing Asset Funds, project-based vouchers and PLHA as sources for the Affordable Housing Strategy (separate record). Compare Carlsbad (15 percent at 7 or more units) and the unincorporated County ordinance (county record). ci.oceanside.ca.us returns 403, but oceanside.legistar.com serves agendas, staff reports and attachments (calendar year selection by form postback).

set.typical_award_size: Amounts vary; no standing developer NOFA. The Council on September 9, 2020 directed an RFP/NOFA implementing the Affordable Housing Strategy with priority to homelessness and extremely low income housing (temporary shelters, bridge housing, vouchers, permanent supportive housing). Funding sources named: HOME entitlement, remaining Housing Asset Funds (former redevelopment), inclusionary in-lieu fees, project-based vouchers and PLHA (PLHA earmarked for emergency shelter operations). The FY 2026-27 Annual Action Plan (approved May 6, 2026) budgets $1,484,745 of HOME (entitlement $467,836, program income $106,909 and $1,037,649 unallocated prior funds) for tenant-based rental assistance, affordable housing development and homeownership gap assistance, with stated targets of 30 TBRA households and 10 to 15 homebuyers rather than a named development project; CDBG entitlement is $1,123,152, mostly rehab, services and Section 108 repayment. The Housing Element set objectives of 634 extremely low income and 1,268 lower income units for 2021-2029.

set.typical_award_size: Requirement, not a subsidy. Housing Element Program 2 commits the City to amend its density bonus ordinance (Zoning Ordinance Article 30) to conform to AB 1763, SB 1227 and AB 2345. State law allows up to a 100 percent bonus for projects reserving at least 15 percent of base units for very low income, 24 percent for lower income or 44 percent for moderate income households. Coastal zone: the certified Article 30 density bonus provisions do not apply to the Downtown District. The Coastal Commission approved the Downtown density amendment (LCP-6-OCN-25-0029-2, 86 units per acre base density, 5,500 unit figure treated as a target) with modifications on February 5, 2026, including a requirement that the City submit updated density bonus regulations covering the Downtown District by January 1, 2029; the Council adopted the modifications (introduced June 3, 2026, ordinance adopted June 17, 2026). Inclusionary in-lieu fee deferral on the same terms as impact fee deferral is available.
set.next_deadline: Applies at entitlement. Confirm the current Zoning Ordinance Article 30 text with Planning; updated density bonus regulations for the Downtown District are due to the Coastal Commission by January 1, 2029.
